this_document: The mock-tool exchange a Pipecat bot speaks with egma's server over HTTPS, as literal requests and answers. The messages are the in-room seam's (mock-tool-exchange.v1.json): the same protocol version, the same hello census and reply, the same tagged tool answer, the same refusal codes and the same answer cap. HTTPS adds the route, the project key, the provider reference that names the simulation, and one refusal the room never needs: a mocked Pipecat Flows function. The egma SDK, egma's API and egma's simulator each test against this file, so a route, a status, a code or a sentence that moves on one side fails a hermetic test on that side. Compare JSON by value; where a `bytes` string is given, the answer body is exactly those bytes.

body.message: This provider reference does not name a live Egma simulation in this API key's project.

not_a_simulation.says: The only answer that makes the SDK inert. Any other 404 — a wrong EGMA_URL, a proxy — is a failure, never inertness.

calendar.says: The simulation most exchanges below run against: its pinned test version mocks two tools, one answering and one failing.

flows.says: A second simulation whose test mocks a Pipecat Flows function, which the hello refuses.

hello.says: Every name the test mocks, in authored order, whether or not the census holds it — the in-room rule. The Flows function in the census is not mocked, so nothing is refused. The stored report also carries first_at and at, which are instants and so are not pinned here.

hello_repeated.says: A second identical hello answers the same. The census is replaced, at moves, first_at is kept.
